ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. Virchow2 (Prism2 slide embedding) is the strongest single model (0.860), clearly ahead of UNI2-h (0.821) and H-optimus-1 (0.830). Metadata alone is weak (0.599) and slightly hurts when added. The tuned member configs differ a lot: Virchow2 wants very strong shrinkage with PCA 16, while the others want L2 normalisation with PCA 128.
REASONING: late_tuned with mean_prob is the most direct and low-variance test of whether the three models carry complementary information. Each member runs at its own best setting and no combination weights are learned, so there is nothing extra to overfit. It gives an anchor point before I explore early, gated and stacking.
EXPECTED: I expect an AUROC of about 0.86-0.87, around or slightly above Virchow2. If it falls below 0.85, the weaker models dilute Virchow2. In that case I would pursue weighted schemes (learned_weights, early_tuned block weights) rather than equal averaging.

ANALYSIS: Late_tuned mean_prob (0.854) is slightly below the virchow2 single baselines (0.860/0.859). Equal averaging seems to dilute Virchow2 with the weaker UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 members, which overlap with each other. Lepidic (0.76) and Papillary (0.77) are the weakest classes.
REASONING: learned_weights can put most or all of the weight on Virchow2 and add the others only where inner CV supports it. This tests directly whether any complementarity exists, using the tuned members. It is cheap, low-variance, and maps the late_tuned region during exploration.
EXPECTED: Expect about 0.86-0.87 AUROC, i.e. at least the Virchow2 level, with gains on Lepidic and Papillary if the other models add signal. If it stays at or below 0.86, the other members add little through probability averaging. I would then try early_tuned, where per-block weights act like per-model shrinkage, and stack.

ANALYSIS: Late_tuned mean_prob (0.854) is below the virchow2-alone baseline (0.860), so equal averaging lets the weaker UNI/H-optimus members dilute Virchow2. Learned weights recovered to 0.864, about the Virchow2 level, which suggests it mostly picks Virchow2. The gain fell just short of the threshold. No early or early_tuned trial has been run yet.
REASONING: We are still exploring, so map the other method families. early_tuned keeps each member's tuned preprocessing and learns block weights by inner CV, so it can down-weight the weaker blocks instead of averaging them. It could also exploit complementary features at the logit level, which late averaging cannot. C=0.01 matches the tuned scale of the UNI and H-optimus members. Virchow2's PCA16 block is small, so at block weight 1 its effective strength would be looser than its tuned 0.001. meta_weight=3 is a middle value.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.86-0.875; a clear gain over trial #1 (>0.011) would be accepted. If it lands at or below 0.855, joint fitting adds nothing beyond Virchow2. I would then test late_tuned stack, or early_tuned with C=0.001, before moving on.

ANALYSIS: Virchow2 alone (0.860) is the strongest; mean_prob fusion (0.854) is dragged down by the weaker UNI2h/H-optimus members. Learned weights recover ~0.864, essentially Virchow2-dominated, and early_tuned at C=0.01 gives 0.858. No method has yet clearly beaten Virchow2 alone. Lepidic and Papillary are the weak classes (~0.76-0.78).
REASONING: Exploration phase: early concatenation is still untested. With balance_blocks, Virchow2's 2560 columns cannot dominate. A strong penalty (C=0.001) with PCA 32 per model and L2 norm matches the regime where the tuned baselines worked (low C, compressed features). Meta_weight 1 is used because metadata alone is weak (0.599).
EXPECTED: AUROC ~0.86-0.87. If early concatenation with balanced blocks matches or beats learned_weights late fusion, the models carry complementary signal that a joint linear model can use. If it falls below ~0.85, joint fitting overfits at n=134 per fold, and late or tuned fusion is the better route.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far lands at about 0.854-0.864 AUROC, close to the best single model (virchow2 at 0.860). Learned_weights (0.8636) likely leans heavily on Virchow2. Lepidic and Papillary stay weak (~0.76-0.78) for every method. The untested methods are gated, late with stacking, and late_tuned with stack or mean_logit.
REASONING: We are still exploring, so the next trial should map a method we have not tried. Stacking on the tuned members' log-probabilities can learn class-specific reweighting, e.g. trusting UNI or H-optimus for particular classes such as Papillary or Lepidic. That is the main way fusion could beat simple averaging here. A strongly regularised stack_C=0.01 limits overfitting with only 134 training patients.
EXPECTED: If complementary per-class information exists, AUROC should reach about 0.87 or higher with gains in Papillary and Lepidic, and be accepted over #1. If it comes in at or below 0.86, the models are largely redundant beyond Virchow2. I would then try gated and early methods only briefly before concluding that fusion gives no clear gain.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far lands at 0.85-0.864, which is about where virchow2 alone sits (0.860). The accepted best, late_tuned mean_prob at 0.854, is actually below virchow2 alone. learned_weights (0.864) likely drifts toward virchow2. Early fusion with balanced blocks reached 0.861. No fusion has yet shown clear complementarity, and Papillary and Lepidic remain the weak classes in every trial.
REASONING: The exploration phase should still cover the untested gated method, which can weight models per patient. A conservative setting suits 134 training patients: PCA 32 per model with L2 normalisation, a small hidden size (32), heavy dropout (0.5), strong weight decay (0.1), 200 epochs, lr 0.001, and 3 seeds. This tells us whether non-linear gating adds anything beyond the linear fusions.
EXPECTED: Expect about 0.84-0.86. Only a value at or above about 0.87 would be a clear gain. If it falls short, I conclude the gated method overfits or adds nothing, and I will drop it in favour of linear early and late variants: early without balance_blocks, mean_logit, and a stronger C.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far lands at 0.85-0.864, about the level of virchow2 alone (0.860). Learned_weights (0.8636) came closest to acceptance but fell just short. Fusion is not clearly adding information beyond Virchow2. UNI2h and H-optimus are weaker and may only dilute it. Untested regions include late fusion with a shared low-dimensional setting, mean_logit, and early fusion without balancing at stronger regularisation.
REASONING: Use an exploration slot to test late_tuned with mean_logit. The geometric mean sharpens agreement and down-weights a member that is uncertain where the others are confident. That differs from mean_prob, which is the current best at 0.8537, so a gain over #1 is plausible. It is cheap and maps the remaining combine options. Weighted_vote is likely worse for AUROC because it discards probability information.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.856-0.865. If it beats #1 by more than ~0.011 it is accepted, and the next steps would be stack with a larger stack_C or early fusion with stronger PCA. If it lands at or below mean_prob, the combine rule is not the bottleneck. Then the remaining hope is early fusion with more regularisation (PCA 16, C 0.0001-0.001), or concluding that Virchow2 alone saturates the signal.

ANALYSIS: Fusion so far is close to, but not above, Virchow2 alone (0.860). Plain averaging (mean_prob, mean_logit) is dragged down by the weaker UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 members. learned_weights (0.8636) came closest to acceptance (+0.0099 vs a 0.0110 threshold). Early, early_tuned, gated and stack all land at 0.851-0.861, and per-class AUROC is nearly identical across methods (Papillary and Lepidic weakest).
REASONING: The generic 'late' method is the main family not yet tested. I will try it with strong shared regularisation (no L2 norm, PCA 16, C=0.001, meta_weight 1), the setting that suited Virchow2. That makes every member heavily shrunk, which may suit the noisy small-n UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 members better than their own tuned PCA128 configs. learned_weights lets the inner CV down-weight weak members. This trial maps the late family and tests whether stronger member shrinkage helps the fusion.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.862-0.868, with a chance of clearing the threshold over trial #1. If it lands at or below 0.86, then the member configuration is not the bottleneck and the fusion is capped near Virchow2 alone. I would then focus on early concatenation with block balancing or on the strength of the late_tuned weights.

ANALYSIS: No fusion has cleared the acceptance threshold. Virchow2 alone (0.860) is about as good as every fusion. The best fusions, learned_weights (0.864) and early with balance_blocks (0.861), only match it, so UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 add little beyond Virchow2. Lepidic and Papillary (about 0.76-0.79) are the weak classes in every trial, so fusion is not fixing the hard classes.
REASONING: Early concatenation with balanced blocks (#4) was competitive at PCA 32 with L2 normalisation. Virchow2's own tuned setting is PCA 16, no L2 and C=0.001. Applying that low-dimensional, heavily regularised setting to every block gives a 48-d fused input, which suits 134 training patients per fold better. Balanced blocks stop any one model dominating. This also maps the PCA and L2 axes for early fusion while we are still in the exploration phase.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.862-0.870, with modest gains in Lepidic and Papillary. If it lands at or below 0.861, low-dimensional early fusion is not the bottleneck. I would then treat the evidence as showing the other models are largely redundant with Virchow2. The remaining budget would go to learned_weights variants or early_tuned with a different C, rather than wider early-fusion sweeps.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far lands at 0.850-0.864, which is statistically indistinguishable from virchow2 alone (0.860). The accepted best, #1 mean_prob at 0.854, is actually below virchow2 alone, so the weaker UNI2-h and H-optimus members dilute it. Learned weights (#2) and early fusion with PCA32 (#4) were the closest to clearing the threshold. Papillary (~0.75) and Lepidic (~0.78) remain the bottleneck classes in every fusion.
REASONING: The last exploration slot should answer an open question about the space: does early fusion on the full embeddings, with no PCA, do better than the PCA-compressed variants? PCA fitted on about 134 patients may throw away fine-grained directions that matter for Papillary and Lepidic. L2-normalising, balancing the blocks and using a strong ridge penalty (C=0.001) keeps the high-dimensional fit regularised. This also maps the pca=None corner, which no trial has touched yet.
EXPECTED: If full-dimensional ridge fusion keeps information that PCA discards, AUROC should reach roughly 0.865-0.875 and gain on Papillary and Lepidic, which could clear the ~0.011 threshold over #1. If it lands near 0.855 again, PCA is not the limiting factor. I would then conclude that fusion is capped near the virchow2 level and concentrate on learned_weights or early_tuned variants that lean on virchow2.

ANALYSIS: All fusions land at 0.850-0.864 AUROC, roughly the level of Virchow2 alone (0.860). Virchow2 dominates, and the accepted best (#1, 0.8537) is actually below it. The closest to acceptance were late_tuned learned_weights (+0.0099) and early with L2 and balanced blocks at C=0.001 (#4 +0.0068, #10 +0.0052). Per-class gaps sit in Lepidic and Papillary (~0.75-0.79), and no method has moved them yet.
REASONING: For early fusion only C=0.001 has been tested, so the regularisation strength is the largest unmapped knob of the most promising family. #10 (L2, no PCA, balanced blocks) is a clean base. Changing only C to 0.01 tells us whether the concatenated model is over-regularised. UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 each preferred C=0.01 alone, and with 3 balanced blocks the effective per-block signal is diluted.
EXPECTED: If under-regularisation was limiting, AUROC should reach about 0.865-0.87, with Lepidic and Papillary improving, and be accepted. If it falls back to around 0.85 or below, early fusion is saturated or overfits at higher C. I would then go back to late_tuned variants (stack with stack_C=0.1, weighted_vote) or early_tuned with meta_weight=1.

ANALYSIS: No fusion has cleared the noise threshold over trial #1 (0.8537). The strongest results are late_tuned learned_weights (0.8636, gain +0.0099 vs threshold 0.011) and early with balanced blocks at C=0.001 (0.8589–0.8606). Across fusions, stronger regularisation helps: early with L2 norm and no PCA scored 0.8589 at C=0.001 versus 0.8463 at C=0.01. Virchow2's tuned C was also the small value 0.001.
REASONING: The C trend in early fusion has not been followed to its end. With about 5.6k standardised columns and only 134 training patients per fold, even stronger shrinkage (C=0.0001) acts like a nearly class-mean-difference classifier. That kind of classifier often maximises AUROC in this p>>n regime. The other settings are kept the same as #10 (L2 norm, no PCA, balanced blocks, meta_weight 1), so this trial cleanly tests the C axis.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.865 or higher, with gains on Acinar, Papillary and Lepidic, and it may be accepted over #1. If it drops below #10, then C=0.001 is the optimum for early fusion. Early fusion would then plateau at roughly Virchow2-alone level, and I would focus on late_tuned/early_tuned variants instead.

ANALYSIS: All fusions sit in 0.846-0.864, essentially at virchow2 alone (0.860). The accepted best (#1, mean_prob, 0.8537) is actually below virchow2, because equal averaging dilutes it. Learned_weights (0.8636) came closest to acceptance, which suggests the gain comes from letting virchow2 dominate. Lepidic and Papillary (~0.75-0.78) are the weak classes for every method.
REASONING: early_tuned has been tried only at C=0.01, which is 10x looser than virchow2's own tuned C=0.001. Its block weights act as per-block C (C·w²), so at C=0.001 virchow2's PCA16 block runs at its own optimal strength. Inner CV can then shrink uni2h and H-optimus1 (w=0.25-0.5) or drop them. This is the most principled untested way to get complementary information without diluting the strongest model. meta_weight=1 matches virchow2's tuned setting.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.862-0.868, with a gain over #1 of roughly +0.01, which may clear the threshold. If it lands at or below about 0.858, early fusion offers no complementarity beyond virchow2. I would then focus on late_tuned variants that weight virchow2 (stack with a looser stack_C, weighted_vote) and accept that fusion is roughly equal to the best single model.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at 0.85-0.86 AUROC, about the level of virchow2 alone (0.860). The best non-accepted gains are learned_weights (+0.0099), early_tuned C=0.001 (+0.0073) and early with L2/PCA32 (+0.0068), all below threshold. Virchow2 likely dominates, and the other two models add little independent signal. Stacking at stack_C=0.01 lost balanced accuracy (0.423), which suggests over-shrinkage that pulls the meta-learner toward the priors.
REASONING: Stacking is the only combiner that can weight models per class, and per-class AUROC differs by model (Lepidic 0.80 and Cribriform 0.88 under stack). Learned_weights showed that adaptive weighting helps, but it uses one global weight per model. A weaker stack penalty (stack_C=0.1) tests whether per-class weighting adds a clear gain once it is not crushed toward the prior. This is an open, plausibly high-variance question, not a tiny tweak of settings already explored.
EXPECTED: If per-class model complementarity is real, I expect AUROC of about 0.865-0.870 with BA recovering to about 0.49 or higher, enough to clear the ~0.011 threshold. If it scores at or below 0.86 or is rejected, stacking is not worth pursuing; I will conclude fusion's ceiling is about virchow2-level and spend only a few more trials, such as early_tuned with other C or meta_weight values, before accepting that no fusion clearly beats the best single model.

ANALYSIS: All fusions land between 0.846 and 0.864, roughly at Virchow2's single-model level (0.860). The closest to acceptance was late_tuned learned_weights (+0.0099 against a 0.011 threshold), likely because it mostly up-weights Virchow2. Stacking, mean_logit and shared-C early fusion add nothing. Lepidic and Papillary (~0.75-0.78) are the weak classes for every method. Gated was tried only once, with moderate regularisation (0.852).
REASONING: Linear fusion variants are close to exhausted and stay inside the noise band. The main open question is whether the gated model, with much stronger regularisation, can exploit per-patient model complementarity. The settings are a smaller projection (hidden 16), PCA 16 (the dimension that suited Virchow2), the strongest weight decay, dropout 0.5 and fewer epochs, which addresses overfitting on 134 patients per fold. This is a different region from trial #6.
EXPECTED: If gating helps, AUROC should be at least 0.865, with gains in Lepidic or Papillary. If it scores at or below about 0.855, the gated route is not worth more budget. I would then return to late_tuned/early_tuned variants that lean on Virchow2, accepting that fusion probably cannot clearly beat Virchow2 alone.

ANALYSIS: Everything clusters at 0.85-0.864, i.e. at the level of virchow2 alone (0.860). No fusion clearly beats the current best #1 (0.8537), which is itself weaker than virchow2. Learned_weights (#2, 0.8636) came closest (+0.0099 vs threshold 0.011), probably by putting most of the weight on virchow2. UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 seem to add little beyond virchow2, and stacking or gating overfits.
REASONING: The remaining untested late_tuned combine is weighted_vote. It is cheap, it completes the map of that method, and like learned_weights it could down-weight the weaker members. The other option, early_tuned at C=0.001 with meta_weight 3 or 10, is close to #13 and #3 and unlikely to move much. Gated and stack configurations are clearly worse. weighted_vote answers an open question for one trial.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.855-0.865. A gain over #1 above about 0.011 would be accepted. Otherwise I would conclude that the combine rule is not the lever, and that fusion offers at most a virchow2-level ceiling with these features. I would then spend the remaining trials on a few early_tuned or early variants (meta_weight 3, pca 64) before accepting that no clear fusion gain exists.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands near the Virchow2-alone level (~0.85-0.864), so the other two models add little. The accepted best (#1, 0.8537) is actually below Virchow2 alone. learned_weights (#2, 0.8636) and early_tuned (#13) came closest to acceptance but stayed below the threshold. Stacking and gating hurt, which is consistent with too few patients to learn a second stage.
REASONING: Late fusion with learned simplex weights is the most promising family. Trial #8 used Virchow2's own setting (no L2, PCA16) for all members, which probably underfits UNI2-h and H-optimus-1. Early fusion with L2 + PCA32 + C=0.001 (#4, 0.8606) was the best shared setting found. Applying that setting inside late learned_weights tests whether members that are better regularized for UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 let the weights find real complementarity.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.863-0.868, which may clear the ~0.011 threshold over #1. If it lands about 0.86 again, then fusion is capped at Virchow2 performance. In that case I would try only one or two more regularization variants before accepting that no fusion clearly beats the best single model.

ANALYSIS: Fusion variants cluster at 0.85-0.86 AUROC. That is the level of virchow2 alone (0.860), and the accepted best #1 (0.854) sits below it. The near-misses are late_tuned learned_weights (+0.0099), early_tuned C=0.001 (+0.0073) and the late/early PCA 16-32, C=0.001 configs (+0.005 to +0.007). Every per-class AUROC stays the same across methods, so the three models seem to carry largely redundant signal. Gated and stacking are consistently worse, as expected with about 134 patients per fold.
REASONING: The strongest variants pair strong shrinkage (C=0.001) and low-dimensional PCA with learned simplex weights, which can lean on virchow2. PCA16 without L2 (#8) and L2 with PCA32 (#17) are both tested, but L2 with PCA16 is not. L2 suited UNI2-h and H-optimus-1, and PCA16 suited virchow2, so this combination could make all three members better regularized at once. It is a cheap, targeted probe of the one region that has come close to the threshold.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.86-0.865, maybe enough to clear the roughly 0.01 threshold over #1. If it lands at about 0.86 and is rejected again, the evidence will show that fusion adds nothing over virchow2 alone. In that case I would spend the remaining trials only on a few untested, clearly different settings, such as early_tuned meta_weight=10 or late_tuned stack stack_C=0.001, and otherwise accept that the stop rule will end the search.

ANALYSIS: All fusions sit in a narrow 0.846-0.864 band. None clearly beats the best single model, virchow2 at 0.860. The accepted best (#1, 0.8537) is actually below virchow2 alone. The near-misses (late_tuned learned_weights 0.8636, early_tuned 0.8611, early L2 0.8589-0.8606) all lean on virchow2 dominating. Stacking and gating hurt, which fits overfitting with 134 training patients.
REASONING: balance_blocks=False has never been tested. Every early trial forced equal block variance, giving virchow2 only a third of the weight. Without balancing, virchow2's 2560 columns give it roughly 45% of the variance, a natural upweighting of the strongest model. UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 still contribute complementary signal (Cribriform, Acinar) under the same shrinkage. To isolate this one knob, I keep the best early settings: L2 on, no PCA, C=0.001, meta_weight 1.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.862-0.868, which could clear the roughly 0.010 threshold against #1. If it lands at or below about 0.860, block weighting is not the bottleneck. That would mean these embeddings carry largely redundant information, so fusion cannot clearly beat virchow2+meta. The remaining budget should then go to only a few targeted checks before the stop rule ends the search.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at about 0.85-0.864 AUROC, which is the level of Virchow2 alone (0.860). The accepted best (#1, mean_prob) is actually below Virchow2 alone. The strongest candidates (late_tuned learned_weights 0.8636, early_tuned C=0.001 0.8611, early PCA32 0.8606) fall just short of the 0.010-0.013 acceptance threshold. Stacking, gated networks and equal-weight combines are consistently worse, which points to small-sample noise and over-weighting of the weaker UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 members.
REASONING: early_tuned improved going from C=0.01 (0.8579) to C=0.001 (0.8611). This trial tests whether stronger global shrinkage continues that trend. Virchow2's own baseline uses C=0.001, and inner-CV block weights can still down-weight the other models. It resolves the open C trend for one of the two near-threshold methods. Only 6 trials remain before the stop rule, so a cheap, directed probe is preferable to more gated or stacking variants.
EXPECTED: Expected AUROC is about 0.860-0.866 with a lower fold SD, perhaps enough to clear the threshold against #1. If it drops below 0.86, C=0.001 is the optimum for early_tuned. That would support concluding that fusion offers no reliable gain over Virchow2+meta, leaving only a late_tuned or late learned_weights variant as a final check.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at 0.851-0.864 AUROC, which is the Virchow2-alone ceiling (0.860). The closest miss was late_tuned learned_weights (0.8636, +0.0099 vs threshold 0.011). Stacking, gating and heavy regularisation are consistently worse, and adding metadata does not help. The other two models seem to add little beyond Virchow2 for these classes.
REASONING: Only 5 trials remain before the stop rule. The best-scoring family is learned simplex weighting of per-model logistic regressions. One untested setting in that family is a moderately larger shared PCA (64) with L2 normalisation at C=0.001. This may let UNI2-h and H-optimus contribute more complementary signal while Virchow2 keeps a strong weight. This is the most plausible remaining route to a gain of about 0.011 over #1, more so than further stack or gated variants, which have trended downward.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.860-0.866 AUROC. If it does not clear the threshold, the conclusion is that fusion gives no reliable gain over Virchow2 on this cohort. The remaining trials would then serve only to confirm this with one or two different configurations before stopping.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants fall between 0.85 and 0.864 AUROC, close to Virchow2 alone (0.860). The best numbers come from late_tuned learned_weights (#2, +0.0099, just under the 0.011 threshold) and from early or early_tuned fusion at C=0.001 (about 0.861). Per-class AUROC barely moves across methods; Papillary and Lepidic stay the weak classes. Fusion appears to sit at a plateau set by Virchow2, and UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 add little complementary signal.
REASONING: Stacking is the one combiner whose behaviour is not yet settled. At stack_C 0.01 and 0.1 it lowered AUROC and especially BA, which looks like overfitting with 134 patients and 21 or more meta-features. stack_C=0.001 is the untested strong-shrinkage end. There the stacker should act like a smoothed, class-specific reweighting of the base log-probabilities, close to learned_weights but allowed to differ per class, which might help Papillary and Lepidic. It is the remaining untested combiner setting with a plausible route to a gain over #1. Only 4 non-improving trials remain before the stop rule, so I prefer it to more near-duplicate early or late C/PCA tweaks.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.855-0.865. A clear accepted gain (>0.01 over #1) is unlikely, but possible if class-specific weighting helps the weak classes. If it lands at or below about 0.86, the stack family is exhausted. That would confirm that no fusion beats the tuned single models by more than noise, and the honest conclusion would be that Virchow2 (or a simple late_tuned average) is the practical choice.

ANALYSIS: All 22 fusion trials sit in a narrow 0.833-0.864 band. None clearly beats Virchow2 alone (0.860), and the accepted best (#1, 0.8537) is itself below Virchow2. The strongest results are late_tuned learned_weights (0.8636), early_tuned meta=1 C=0.001 (0.8611) and early with L2 + PCA32 (0.8606), all just under the acceptance threshold. Stacking, gated networks and geometric means hurt, consistent with overfitting at 134 training patients and Virchow2 dominating.
REASONING: early_tuned is the most principled linear fusion: per-block weights act as per-model C, which lets Virchow2 dominate while UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 add small corrections. Its best setting so far (C=0.001, meta=1) has an untested neighbour at meta_weight=3. In #3, meta=3 was paired with a worse C (0.01), so the effect of metadata weight at the good C is still open. This is a cheap, targeted probe of the one method that still has unexplored, plausibly useful settings.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC of about 0.860-0.866, with possible small gains on Papillary/Acinar if age/sex carries some signal. If it does not clear the about 0.011 threshold, I conclude that three-model fusion offers no reliable gain over Virchow2+meta on this data, and that the remaining differences are fold noise.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands between 0.85 and 0.861, about the level of virchow2 alone (0.8601). None has cleared the acceptance threshold over #1 (0.8537). The learned_weights variants reach about 0.860 but carry large thresholds (0.018-0.021), probably because the inner-CV weight selection adds variance. Stacking and gating are clearly worse.
REASONING: With two trials left before the stop rule, the best remaining bet is a low-variance combiner on members that are individually stronger than the tuned uni2h and hoptimus1 baselines. The shared setting L2 normalisation, PCA 32, C=0.001 did well in both early (#4) and late with learned weights (#17). Pairing it with fixed mean_prob avoids the variance of learned weights. This could keep the about 0.86 level while narrowing the paired SE enough to clear the threshold over #1.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.860-0.865 with a threshold near 0.008-0.011, which would be a borderline accept. If it lands at or below about 0.858, or is rejected, I will conclude that fusion adds nothing measurable beyond virchow2 alone and that the fused AUROC is capped near 0.86.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at 0.85-0.864 AUROC, which is about the level of virchow2 alone (0.860). The best non-accepted results are late_tuned learned_weights (0.8636) and early or early_tuned at C=0.001 (about 0.861). None clears the roughly 0.01 noise threshold over #1 (0.8537). Stacking and heavily regularised gating hurt. Per-class AUROC barely moves: Lepidic and Papillary stay around 0.75-0.79 in every method.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the stop rule. Early fusion with L2 norm, balanced blocks and C=0.001 is the most consistent family (0.8589-0.8606), and its scores vary with PCA size. PCA=32 and PCA=None are tested; PCA=64 sits between them and is untested. It keeps more per-model signal than 32 while still cutting the dimension enough to curb overfitting, so it is the most plausible remaining shot at about 0.865 or more.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.860-0.866, which would likely be accepted if the paired gain over #1 exceeds about 0.01. If it is rejected, I conclude that fusion saturates at the virchow2 single-model level on this data. The extra models add no reliable signal beyond the noise threshold, and virchow2+meta, or a simple fusion, should be reported as equivalent.
